## Data Simulation

We use the R package `splatter` to simulate scRNA-seq data to be analyzed in this example.

```{r simulation, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(splatter)

seed <- 1234
set.seed(seed)

params <- newSplatParams(
  # see: https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/splatter/inst/doc/splat_params.html
  
  seed=seed,
  
  nGenes=500,
  batchCells=1000,
  
  # cell types
  group.prob=1, # only 1 true cell population
  
  # library size (= counts per cell)
  lib.loc=10,
  lib.scale=0.2,
  
  # dropout probabilities
  dropout.type="experiment",
  dropout.mid=50,
  dropout.shape=5e-2,
  
  # differential expression
  de.prob=0.01,
  de.downProb=0.5,
  de.facLoc=0.4,
  de.facScale=0.4,
)

sim <- splatSimulate(
  params,
  method="groups",
  verbose=FALSE
)
count_data <- counts(sim)
count_data <- as(count_data, "CsparseMatrix") # for seurat

true_idents <- as.factor(substr(colData(sim)$Group, 6, 10))
```

We use `Seurat` to obtain an initial clustering and save UMAP embeddings for later plotting.

```{r initial_idents, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(Seurat)

seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts=count_data)
seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
seurat_obj <- ScaleData(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
seurat_obj <- RunPCA(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
seurat_obj <- FindNeighbors(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
seurat_obj <- FindClusters(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
seurat_obj <- RunUMAP(seurat_obj, dims=1:10, verbose=FALSE)

umap <- Embeddings(seurat_obj, reduction="umap")
initial_idents <- Idents(seurat_obj)
```

## StabCell

For StabCell we first need to define a clustering and a testing function which are applied to the individual subsamples. We once again use `Seurat` functions for this.

```{r cluster_fn}
cluster_fn <- function(data, subsample_indices=NULL, cluster_args=NULL){
  seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts=data)
  seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
  seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
  seurat_obj <- ScaleData(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
  seurat_obj <- RunPCA(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
  seurat_obj <- FindNeighbors(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
  seurat_obj <- FindClusters(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
  identities <- Idents(seurat_obj)
  return(identities)
}

marker_fn <- function(data, identities, weights, cluster_id1, cluster_id2=NULL, marker_args=NULL){
  # cannot test cluster against itself
  # --> check for cluster collision
  if((!is.null(cluster_id2)) && (cluster_id1 == cluster_id2)){
    p_values <- rep(1., nrow(data))
    names(p_values) <- rownames(data)
    return(p_values)
  } else {
    # prepare seurat object
    seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts=data)
    seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj, verbose=FALSE)
    Idents(seurat_obj) <- identities
    
    markers <- FindMarkers(
      seurat_obj, ident.1=cluster_id1, ident.2=cluster_id2, test.use="wilcox",
      logfc.threshold=0.0, min.pct=0., # no pre-selection of genes
      verbose=FALSE
    )
    
    # format results
    p_values <- markers$p_val_adj
    names(p_values) <- rownames(markers)
  }
  
  return(p_values)
}
```

If you want to make use of StabCell's parallelization, you need to register `doFuture` with an appropriate plan as your backend.

```{r parallel, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
# library(doFuture)
# library(RhpcBLASctl)
# 
# blas_set_num_threads(4)
# plan(multicore, workers=50)
# registerDoFuture()
```

We can now run StabCell. Using `progressr`'s `with_progress()` will display progress bars.

```{r stabcell, warning=FALSE}
library(StabCell)
library(progressr)

with_progress({
  stabcell_results <- StabCell(
      data=count_data,
      reference_identities=initial_idents,
      cluster_fn=cluster_fn,
      marker_fn=marker_fn,
      assumption="r_concavity",
      PFER_max=25,
      subsampling_iterations=50,
      marker_global=TRUE,
      marker_local=FALSE,
      packages=c("Seurat"),    # packages that are needed for clustering or testing
      verbose=TRUE
    )
})
```

## Results

StabCell returns many intermediate results, which may come in handy. Let's have a look!

```{r list_results}
names(stabcell_results)
```

We can compare the different clusterings...

```{r plot_clusterings, fig.width=8, fig.height=6, out.width="100%"}
library(ggplot2)

plot_clustering <- function(coords, idents, title=""){
  if(length(idents) == 0){ idents <- rep("0", nrow(coords)) }
  p_umap <- ggplot() +
    geom_point(data=coords, mapping=aes(x=umap_1, y=umap_2, color=idents), size=0.1) +
    theme_void() + 
    theme(legend.position="none") +
    labs(title=title)
  p_hist <- ggplot() +
    geom_bar(data=data.frame(Cluster=idents), mapping=aes(x=Cluster, fill=Cluster)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(legend.position="none", panel.grid=element_blank()) +
    labs(y="# Cells") +
    coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, nrow(coords)))
  return(p_umap / p_hist)
}

p_true <- plot_clustering(coords=umap, idents=true_idents, title="True Clustering")
p_init <- plot_clustering(coords=umap, idents=initial_idents, title="Initial Clustering")
p_stabcell <- plot_clustering(coords=umap, idents=stabcell_results$stable_clustering, title="Stable Clustering")
p_true | p_init | p_stabcell
```

… see how stable the individual clusters are …

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=4, out.width="100%"}
ggplot(
  data=data.frame(
    cluster=stabcell_results$stable_clustering,
    cell_stability_score=stabcell_results$cell_stability_score
  ),
  mapping=aes(fill=cluster, y=cell_stability_score, x=cluster)
) +
  geom_violin() +
  labs(y="Cell Stability Score", x="StabCell Cluster") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0, 1)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position="none",
    panel.grid.minor=element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x=element_blank()
  )
```

... and inspect the stable markers.

```{r stable_markers}
stabcell_results$stable_markers_global |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, desc(selection_freq)) |>
  knitr::kable() |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed")) |>
  kableExtra::scroll_box(width="100%")
```

#### Conclusion

-   The naive clustering generates many spurious clusters.
-   StabCell can reduce the number of spurious clusters.
-   All StabCell clusters are unstable and should be treated with care.
-   For each of the remaining spurious clusters we observe fewer than the specified `PFER_max = 25` markers, which should also be treated with care due to the unstable clustering.
